title: He Is A Brave Warrior, Who Conquers
subtitle: Siree Raag · Ang 86
summary: This shabad opens with o Nanak, he is a brave warrior, who conquers and subdues his vicious inner ego. It turns the heart toward o Nanak, without the Name, everything is painful, and happiness is forgotten.
whyItMatters: It matters when life feels inflated, defensive, and self-protective because the shabad keeps ego inside remembrance, conduct, and the Creator's larger care instead of private momentum.
takeaway: Keep returning to this turn: O Nanak, without the Name, everything is painful, and happiness is forgotten.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਸੋ ਸੂਰਾ ਵਰੀਆਮੁ ਜਿਨਿ ਵਿਚਹੁ ਦੁਸਟੁ ਅਹੰਕਰਣੁ ਮਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: naanak so sooraa vareeaam jin vichahu dhusaT aha(n)karan maariaa ||
lines.translation: O Nanak, he is a brave warrior, who conquers and subdues his vicious inner ego.
Praising the Naam, the Name of the Lord, the Gurmukhs redeem their lives.

lines.gurmukhi: ਆਪਿ ਹੋਆ ਸਦਾ ਮੁਕਤੁ ਸਭੁ ਕੁਲੁ ਨਿਸਤਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: aap hoaa sadhaa mukat sabh kul nisataariaa ||
lines.translation: They themselves are liberated forever, and they save all their ancestors.
Those who love the Naam look beauteous at the Gate of Truth.
The self-willed manmukhs die in egotism-even their death is painfully ugly.

lines.gurmukhi: ਸਭੋ ਵਰਤੈ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਕਿਆ ਕਰਹਿ ਵਿਚਾਰਿਆ ॥
lines.transliteration: sabho varatai hukam kiaa kareh vichaariaa ||
lines.translation: Everything happens according to the Lord's Will; what can the poor people do?
Attached to self-conceit and duality, they have forgotten their Lord and Master.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਨਕ ਬਿਨੁ ਨਾਵੈ ਸਭੁ ਦੁਖੁ ਸੁਖੁ ਵਿਸਾਰਿਆ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naanak bin naavai sabh dhukh sukh visaariaa ||1||
lines.translation: O Nanak, without the Name, everything is painful, and happiness is forgotten. ||1||

structure: It opens by naming the condition without ornament: o Nanak, he is a brave warrior, who conquers and subdues his vicious inner ego.
The middle movement widens the correction through the self-willed manmukhs die in egotism-even their death is painfully ugly.
It closes with a return you can actually keep: o Nanak, without the Name, everything is painful, and happiness is forgotten.
